newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs unshaken by upbeat EPA report.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs unshaken by upbeat EPA report.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures drifted lower in late Friday trade after largely ignoring an upbeat monthly report by Japan's Economic Planning Agency (EPA), dealers said.
The EPA said Japan's economy was firming up and its own assessment of the economy was half a step more optimistic than last month.

"People were just not interested in the EPA report. Although the bias is to the topside in the Japanese interest rate market, it's been very quiet for the last few weeks," a trader with an Asian institution said.
"The Japanese economy and monetary policy are going to remain low for quite some time and that's seen in the JGBs and Euroyen," a local bank dealer said.
The lead March Euroyen contract stood at 99.00 at 1115 GMT after trading a 99.00-99.06 range against its IMM close at 99.03. Volume was 11,000 lots.
The trader at the Asian institution said the contract was within a technical congestion zone.
"We would sell around 99.03. There's a potential risk of reaching 99.10 but I can't see it happening. And any spooks to the market could easily see a move to the downside of 10 ticks," he said.
He said JGB futures were trading on the higher end in line with bullishness in global long-end futures contracts.
"They'll be well bought on dips but it will be hard to grind higher," he said, adding that supply concerns and technical factors were likely to thwart further rises.
September JGBs ended at 124.85 against their previous 124.93 after hitting a high of 125.07.
Eurodollar futures were stuck in tight ranges amid thin trade ahead of the U.S. June Producer Price Index (PPI), due at 1230 GMT.
The PPI is expected to be flat for June and up 0.1 percent without its more volatile food and energy components, according to economists' forecasts.
September Eurodollars ended at 94.235 against their IMM close at 94.230.
